content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `height` of length `n`. There are `n` vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of the `i`-th line are `(i, 0)` and `(i, height[i])`.

Choose two distinct indices `i` and `j` (0-based) with `i < j`. The container formed by the lines at `i` and `j` and the x-axis holds an amount of water equal to `min(height[i], height[j]) * (j - i)`. Output the largest amount of water a container can store.

You may not tilt the container. Design an algorithm that runs in linear time and uses constant extra space.
constraints: Expected time complexity: O(n); expected extra space: O(1).
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array containing one array: [[h0,h1,h2,...]]. Example: [[1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7]]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized integer representing the maximum area, e.g. 49
notes: Use the two-pointer greedy approach: start with pointers at both ends and move the pointer at the shorter wall inward.
Area uses the smaller of the two heights times the distance between indices.
This problem is intended to reject O(n^2) brute-force solutions for large n.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Best pair is indices 1 and 8 (0-based): min(8,7) * (8-1) = 7 * 7 = 49.

hidden.label: Large flat region (single generated stress case)

notes: Generator-style testcases (tc_31, tc_32) are provided in JavaScript generator-string format. The judge harness must expand these generator expressions into concrete arrays before running submissions.

For each generated input array the harness must compute the expected integer output using a trusted reference implementation (two-pointer O(n) algorithm) and compare submission outputs to those values.

Generators produce multiple concrete inputs (count entries). The judge should treat each generated input as an independent test within the batch and award the testcase weight only if all generated inputs in that batch match expected outputs.
Generator distributions are weighted to exercise a variety of structural patterns (increasing, decreasing, plateau, alternating, symmetric, peaks) to catch heuristic/greedy mistakes.
All concrete testcases compare integer equality.
Input parsing must accept the documented JSON array format. For generator cases the harness will provide expanded concrete inputs to the submission.

solution.approach: Two-pointer greedy: initialize left pointer at 0 and right pointer at n-1. Compute area = min(height[left], height[right]) * (right - left). Move the pointer at the shorter wall inward (if height[left] < height[right] then left++ else right--). Track and return the maximum area seen. This runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) extra space.
